about.title: Baldwin Park Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Baldwin Park sits along the I-10 (San Bernardino Freeway) in Los Angeles County, and a good share of the work that happens here happens in motion: delivery routes down Ramona Boulevard, warehouse shifts off Baldwin Park Boulevard, construction crews working near Francisquito Avenue. When someone gets hurt on the clock, the first question is usually about workers' compensation. Under California law, that system is normally your only remedy against your employer, and it pays regardless of who was at fault. It does not, however, close the door on everyone else. If a subcontractor, a property owner, an equipment manufacturer, or another driver caused your injury, a separate claim against that third party may be available. Public records show 406 injury collisions in Baldwin Park in 2025, with 584 people hurt, and some of those crashes involved people simply doing their jobs. We handle workplace injury and third-party claims in Baldwin Park, and we work on contingency — no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Baldwin Park Workers Choose Us

items.title: Two Claims, Not One
items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but California law allows a separate injury claim against a negligent third party. We can review whether both apply to your situation.

items.title: Deadlines That Matter
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a work injury to your employer, and third-party injury claims carry a two-year deadline. Early guidance helps keep both windows open.

items.title: Protection From Retaliation
items.desc: It is illegal in California for an employer to punish you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. We can explain your rights if you feel pressure at work after getting hurt.

items.question: I was hit on the I-10 while making deliveries for my Baldwin Park employer. Is that only a workers' comp case?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Because you were working, workers' compensation would typically cover your medical care and part of your lost wages no matter who caused the crash. If another driver was at fault, though, California law also lets you pursue a separate injury claim against that driver. We can review both so nothing is left on the table.

items.question: What happens if I miss the 30-day window to tell my employer?
items.answer: California asks you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days. Missing that mark can complicate a workers' compensation claim, but it does not automatically end it, and it has no effect on a third-party claim, which runs on its own two-year deadline. Report as soon as you can and speak with us about where things stand.

items.question: Do you charge anything, and are you a law firm?
items.answer: We work on contingency, which means there is no fee unless there is a recovery. Contact us for a free case review of your workplace injury claim.
